naslov: The Spiritual Provision of the Believer

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.

segmenti.tekst: Praise and thanks belong to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

Thanks be to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, who has honoured us to gather here tonight in His name, in order to begin a series of lectures entitled "Zad al-'Ibad", or the soul's, or the spiritual, provision of the believer.

And the best thing for a person, a Muslim, to occupy himself with is seeking Islamic knowledge. And we spoke about this a few Fridays ago: that a person can earn Jannah (Paradise) by seeking Islamic knowledge.

The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Man salaka tariqan yaltamisu fihi 'ilman sahhalallahu lahu tariqan ilal-jannah" – whoever follows a path in seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Jannah. How so, dear brothers?

Because, through that knowledge, he will know how to walk that path to Jannah. And there is no better knowledge than knowledge of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. You know well that iman (faith), or what a person believes, is nothing without deeds.

Without deeds it is nothing. There are many people who say: "We believe with the heart," but there are no deeds, no deeds at all. That is also what the mushrikun, the polytheists, said in the time of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: "وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ" – He says: if you were to ask them who created the heavens and the Earth, what would they answer? They would say: "Allah created it."

"Allah created it", that is, they affirmed the existence of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, but they did not know how to worship Him, and so they fell into errors, into polytheism, into unbelief. So Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, to explain to people how to worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in what way to worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. That is why it is very important for a person to know the truth, or the reality, of iman, or belief. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in some Qur'anic verses describes iman,

that is, He mentions some of the pillars of iman, as, for example, in Surah Al-Baqarah, where He says: "The Messenger Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, believes in what is revealed to him, and those who are with him believe", that is, the believers believe.

"All of them believe in Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in His angels, in His books, His messengers, and they make no distinction between the messengers" – and they make no distinction between the messengers – "wa qalu sami'na wa ata'na" – and they say: we hear and we obey – "ghufranaka" – we seek Your forgiveness, my Lord,
"and to You we shall all return." If we analyse this verse more closely, dear brothers, we see how beautifully Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, arranged these pillars of iman, these conditions of iman.

He began first with iman, or belief in Him, subhanahu wa ta'ala, which is the foundation. A person cannot be a believer if he does not believe in Allah. After that He mentions the angels. After that He mentions the angels – why? Because the angels are the link between Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and His creatures.
After that He mentions the books of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, which are also a link between Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and His messengers. And after that He mentions the messengers.

And who brings these books? The angels, that is, the angel Jibril. That is how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, arranged, arranged, arranged these conditions of iman. And finally, as we said, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions the messengers, who are the link between Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and His creatures.

So much for the verse. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, speaks a little more about iman, that is, a little more extensively, in his hadiths. In the hadith narrated by Abu Hurayrah, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu (may Allah be pleased with him), it is mentioned that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was sitting one day with people in his, in his mosque.
And a man came. In the hadith it is mentioned that a man came in exceptionally white clothing. No traces, it says, of travel could be seen on him, and none of the companions knew him.

He sat down by the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and asked him: "Tell me," he says, "what is iman, what is iman, O Messenger of Allah, what is belief?" The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Al-imanu an tu'mina billahi wa mala'ikatihi wa kutubihi wa bi liqa'ihi wa rusulihi wa tu'mina bil-ba'th" – he says: iman is that you believe in Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala – that you believe that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and that you believe that He is the Creator of everything,

that He governs everything, that He gives life and death, that He is the One who determines the destiny of His creatures. That we believe in the angels. We must believe in the angels, whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, created from light.

That we believe in Jibril, that Jibril brought the revelation to the prophets. That we believe in Mika'il, who is in charge of the rain. That we believe in Malik, who is in charge of Jahannam (Hellfire).

That we believe in Israfil, who blows the horn, that is, who will blow the horn when the Day of Judgement comes. That we believe in Malak al-Mawt (the Angel of Death), who takes the souls of people, or of creatures. That we believe in Munkar and Nakir, who will question people,

in the Kiraman Katibin, who record a person's good and bad deeds. That we believe in Allah's books [unclear] to the prophets, such as the Zabur (Psalms), which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent – to whom did Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, send the Zabur? To Dawud, alayhis-salam (peace be upon him). That we believe in the Tawrat (Torah), which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent to Musa, alayhis-salam.

That we believe in the Injil (Gospel), which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, revealed to Isa, alayhis-salam. That we believe in the Qur'an, dear brothers, and that we believe that the Qur'an has remained unchanged from the time of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, until this very day and that it will remain unchanged until the Day of Judgement, because Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, promises us this with the words: "Indeed, We have revealed this Qur'an and indeed We will guard it from alteration."

Indeed, We have sent down this Qur'an, revealed this Qur'an to Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and indeed We will guard it, guard it from alteration. After that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: that a person should believe in the meeting with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. All of us should believe in the meeting, in the meeting with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, when we stand before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and give account, give account, and give account. He further says, subhanahu wa ta'ala… the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, further says: and that a person believe in the messengers – that a person believe that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala,

sent messengers to people, and there is no people to whom Allah did not send a messenger, to warn them, to call them to the worship of Allah, to call them to the worship of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Wa laqad ba'athna fi kulli ummatin rasulan ani'budullaha wajtanibut-taghut" – and to every people We sent, sent a messenger. There is no people to whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, did not send a messenger. Some believed, some did not. What we know is that the people of Yunus believed,

and so Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, saved them from punishment in this dunya (this world). That we believe in those 25 prophets whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentioned in the Qur'an. That we believe that the best prophets, that is, the best 5 prophets, are the Ulul-'Azm: Nuh, alayhis-salam, Isa, Musa, Ibrahim, and Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

And that the best of them is Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, the seal of all the prophets, the seal of all the prophets, and that after him there is no prophet. That after Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, there is no prophet.

It is our obligation to believe this. This is our belief, dear brothers. This is our belief. And we must all, we must all know this, these, these… basics. Also, also, that a person believe in the resurrection.

That a person believe in the resurrection, that he will be resurrected. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "La uqsimu bi yawmil-qiyamah" – I swear, or I take an oath, by the Day of Resurrection – "wa la uqsimu bin-nafsil-lawwamah" – and I swear by the self-reproaching soul – "ayahsabul-insanu allan najma'a 'izamah" – He says: does man think that We will not gather his bones? "Ayahsabul-insanu allan najma'a 'izamah." And so the verses go on, until Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "ila Rabbika yawma'idhinil-mustaqarr" –

and you will all return to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, you will all return to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. And a person must believe, a person must believe that we will, that we will return to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. After that this man asked the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam: "What is, what is Islam?" The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "An ta'budallaha wa la tushrika bihi shay'an" – he says: that you worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and do not ascribe partners to Him, that you do not worship alongside Him other, other false deities.

He goes on: "wa tuqimas-salata" – and that you perform the prayer – "wa tu'tiyaz-zakatal-mafrudata wa tasuma Ramadan" – and that you give the zakat and fast the month, the month of Ramadan. This man further says: "Mal-ihsan?" – he says: what is ihsan, or excellence in doing good? The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "An ta'budallaha ka'annaka tarahu, fa in lam takun tarahu fa innahu yarak" – he says: ihsan is that you worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, as if you see Him,
for if you do not see Him, He certainly sees you. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in another verse: "Vision does not reach Him, but He reaches all vision."

And this is the highest degree of faith. So we see, dear brothers, how the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, ordered this beautiful religion of ours: in the first place, that is, the first degree of our religion, is Islam.

Those are the outward deeds, what a person does, from the shahadah (testimony of faith) to the Hajj. Isn't that so? Meaning, what a person does with his limbs – outward deeds. After that, a somewhat higher degree is iman, or belief –

the deeds of the heart. And the last and highest degree is al-ihsan, excellence: that one worships Allah, that a person worships Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, as if he sees Him. How beautifully, how exquisitely the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, put it!

Meaning, it certainly cannot be put more beautifully than this. Now, having explained belief, there arises, there arises, dear brothers, a logical question, there arises a logical question: is iman only that a person, that is, that a person believes with his heart, while there is nothing of it in his deeds?

That is not iman. That is completely incorrect, and it is very widespread among our people, unfortunately: that someone says: "I believe with my heart, and deeds are not important." This talk, or what these particular people say, is refuted by Qur'anic verses and many hadiths.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: and when Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, reveals a surah to His Messenger, He says, the munafiqun (hypocrites)… the munafiqun said this, [unclear]: "Whose iman," they say, "has this surah increased? Whose iman has this surah increased?" "Fa ammal-ladhina amanu fa zadathum imanan wa hum yastabshirun" – but, He says, as for the believers, the mu'minun, He says, this surah raises their iman, increases their iman, and they rejoice.
وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَتْهُمْ رِجْسًا إِلَىٰ رِجْسِهِمْ وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كَافِرُونَ
segmenti.prevod: “But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it adds filth to their filth, and they die while they are disbelievers.” (At-Tawbah 9:125)

segmenti.tekst: But, He says, for those who do not believe, this, He says, this surah adds doubt and unbelief to the unbelief in which they already were.

And they will die, that is, they will die as unbelievers, they will die as unbelievers. So we see that this verse clearly says, dear brothers, that iman sometimes increases and sometimes decreases; that is, iman is that a person testifies with the heart and the tongue and implements it with deeds,

proves it with deeds. Iman is not only that a person says: "I believe," and turns his head away from worship and the other things that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has commanded His servants. Also, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an, He says: "Truly the true believers are those whose hearts," He says, "tremble with fear when Allah's name is mentioned, and," He says, "when Allah's verses are recited to them,

zadathum imana" – He says: it increases their iman, which clearly indicates that iman increases and decreases in a person. Also, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Al-imanu bid'un wa sab'una shu'bah" – he says: iman consists of sixty-some branches, and in another hadith, he says, of seventy-some branches. He says: "A'laha qawlu la ilaha illallah" – he says: the greatest part of iman, the greatest part of iman is, are the words "La ilaha illallah", there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. He says: and that a person removes from the road what harms people.

So we see that a deed is part of iman: if you remove from the road something that harms people – isn't that so? – that is part of iman, part of good belief. See how our beautiful religion teaches us not to do, not to commit evil to anyone; rather, how Allah rewards us and tells us, through His Messenger, that it is part of iman that we remove what harms people, that we remove it with our own hands – that this is part of iman.

Also, we mentioned a hadith narrated by Abdullah ibn Abbas, in which the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says – that is, he narrates that a delegation of the tribe of Abd al-Qays came to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

And they said, that is, they asked to enter to see the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "Who are these people?" And they informed him, saying: "O Messenger, these are Rabi'ah." Rabi'ah is the father of this Abd al-Qays, after whom this tribe got its name.

And the Prophet knew very well, he knew very well that nasab, or lineage, of those tribes. So he said: "Marhaban bil-qawmi ghayra khazaya wa la nadama." Here the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, praises this people, he says: "Welcome, welcome, O delegation, or O people, who have accepted Islam and were not late in accepting Islam, and did not fight against the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam,

and were not taken captive by the Muslims." And they say: "O Messenger, we have come to you here today, and," they say, "we can only come in the months when fighting is forbidden," that is, in the months when the Arabs did not wage war.

Those are the months of Rajab, Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram. In those months the Arabs did not wage war. So they used that opportunity to come to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, so that the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, would

explain to them some things related to the religion, some things related to the religion. And between them and the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, lived a tribe called Mudar. And between them wars constantly, constantly broke out.

There was constant fighting. So they came to the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, only in the months when fighting was forbidden. And they say: "O Messenger, command us something that we will apply and pass on to our people to do, so that they may enter Jannah."

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "I will command you four things, and I will forbid you four things." The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "The first thing I command you is iman billah, belief in Allah." After that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Hal tadruna mal-imanu billah?" – he says: "Do you know what iman in Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is?" They say: "Allah and His Messenger know best, best, best."

Pay attention now to this hadith, or to the end of this hadith. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Iman is that you testify that there is no other deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is His Messenger,

that you perform the prayer." See how the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says that performing the prayer is part of iman. And, by Allah, no one can come to the dawn prayer (Fajr) except the one whose iman is strong. Can anyone come to the Fajr prayer, or to the night prayer (Isha), when that Isha is late and a person would rather sleep – except the one whose iman is strong?
Can the one whose iman is weak come to the noon prayer (Dhuhr) and lock up his shop? He cannot. Only a person of strong iman can do that. The Prophet further says: "and that you give zakat".

Is giving zakat not part of iman? And no one can give zakat except the one whose iman is strong. There are people who do not give zakat. And zakat – if a person denies zakat, then the funeral prayer (janazah) is not prayed for him.
The janazah is not prayed for him. If he refuses to give it, while testifying that zakat is obligatory, then, meaning, if he is in an Islamic state, he must give it.

There is no other way. And no one gives zakat except the one who has strong iman. Because there are people who have millions – now you have to set aside so much money to give zakat. That, by Allah, only a person of strong iman can do.

Only a person of strong, strong iman can. Also, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: it is part of iman that a person fasts the month of Ramadan. Now it is easy to fast, the winter days have come, it is very easy to fast.

But, by God, when it was summer, you could count on your fingers who was fasting and who was not. And no one can fast in those hot summer days except the one who has strong iman. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says at the end of this hadith, he says: it is part of iman that you give a fifth of what you have taken as spoils of war, that you give a fifth to the categories to whom it is given, meaning to Allah, His Messenger, the relatives, the orphans, the poor and, finally, those who fight in the way of Allah.
Why did he tell them all this? Because between them and this tribe of Mudar those battles constantly broke out and wars constantly broke out, so they would sometimes take these spoils of war.

We see, dear brothers, that iman is not only that a person testifies with the heart; rather, iman is that a person testifies with the heart, also confirms it with words, and implements it, or proves it, with his deeds.

That is iman. Iman increases and decreases. When a person sins – and a person can feel this in himself – when a person sins, iman drops, it isn't even at 1%. When a person does a deed with which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is pleased, he clearly feels that it is strong.

And it has surely happened, you know it yourselves: during Ramadan there are constantly some acts of worship. We see, meaning, tarawih, then after tarawih the night prayer, then the Fajr prayer, then a lesson (dars) – and you feel as if you are flying.

When a person goes on umrah, likewise, he comes back as if he has come from another dimension: full of iman, full of enthusiasm, full of strength. And when a person commits sins, when he is in bad company, when he is in bad places, when he gives himself over to vices, then iman drops, it is gone.

And that is why, dear brothers, a person should do things that increase his iman, that increase his belief. Also, these gatherings of ours here increase iman too. Because we hear something good, we hear something wise, we hear something that will benefit us. And all of this, in sha Allah, that we will do further, are the foundations of our beautiful religion,
it is part of belief, and after that prayer and so on, good character (akhlaq) – so that a person has something to return with to the Lord, to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
